title: Latest successful backup with database context
description: For each database that has a successful backup, return only the latest successful backup by finished_seq. If several successful backups for the same database share the maximum finished_seq, choose the row with the larger backup_id. Return exactly five columns: database_name, hostname, owner_role, finished_seq, size_mb. Sort by database_name ASC.
starter_sql:
SELECT d.name AS database_name, s.hostname, r.role_name AS owner_role, b.finished_seq, b.size_mb
FROM backups AS b
hints: An anti-join can prove that no later successful backup exists for the same database.
When finished_seq ties, the backup with the larger id is considered later for this task.
solution_explanation: A self LEFT JOIN removes every successful row that has a later candidate; the remaining joins add context.
